summary: BifrOSt has shell-owned home-screen and Today widgets (a fixed set of nine kinds, with small and medium sizes, a Smart Stack and an Add Widget gallery) and Control Center toggles, all drawn by the shell. There is no app-facing WidgetKit equivalent: apps cannot ship a widget extension, a timeline provider, a Live Activity, an app-provided control, or a widget intent. The SDK widgets module is a drawing kit for app windows, not a widget API.

features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/widget_kind.rs; springboard/src/shell/services/widgets_timeline.rs (register, sync_manifests); springboard/sdk/src/widgets_timeline.rs (Kind, register); springboard/src/shell/apphost.rs (Manifest::widgets); springboard/ui/src/widget_kind.rs (parse_manifest); springboard/src/shell/services/widgets_timeline.rs (opened_body); springboard/src/shell/notify/center.rs (open_widget sends opened); springboard/sdk/src/widgets_timeline.rs (EVENT_OPENED, Event::Opened)
features.note: The widget kind registry (identifiers, sizes, bundles, lookups by size) is tested headless in springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-tests-10-w7.rs. Not wired into apps or the shell, and not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Widgets are compiled into the shell. No app can register a widget kind, and there is no bundle or extension process. Built 2026-10-19: an app registers the widget kinds it offers, either with the widgets_timeline service call register (SDK Kind and register: id, name, description, sizes) or as [[widget]] tables in manifest.toml (id, name, description, families, configurable), which the shell reads for every installed app and registers on its tick. features.note: Xcode tooling. BifrOSt has host previews (bifrost pc smoke APP) for app windows, not for widgets.

gaps: No separate widget extension process: apps register kinds (register or [[widget]] tables) and answer reload events themselves; the reference starts its widget provider on demand as a non-UI process (REA ev_d82b017aac4f432ec976df4928ec940780c5d05f5810e2933bc924c4be404569 (WidgetKit Info.plist: the widget extension point runs as an on-demand non-UI process hosted by the system)). There is no WidgetBundle or declarative configuration type for apps (widget_kind::WidgetBundle exists as a model only).
Widget buttons run over the app's control socket, so the app must be running; there is no start-on-demand extension (Button, Toggle and AppIntent inside a widget extension).
WidgetCenter reload calls exist (reload_timelines, reload_all_timelines, current_configurations) but there is no reload budget like the reference's daily limit.
No declarative widget view tree (stacks, images, shapes, gradients): a widget row is title, value, detail, buttons, per-size variants and a background colour.
No tinted widget look: the accented and vibrant modes and widgetAccentable exist only as a model (springboard/ui/src/widget_render.rs); the shell always draws widgets in full colour.
The shell's own built-in home-screen and Today tiles are pixel images without accessibility elements (app widgets are exported to the element map and AT-SPI).
Widget location and network grants are a model only (springboard/ui/src/widget_access.rs); nothing enforces them, because no widget process exists to confine.
The home-screen grid (homeconf) places only the shell's own kinds; third-party widgets live in the Notification Centre column.
